definition: A specific form of data contamination where synthetic training data inadvertently incorporates content derived from benchmark test sets.
details: This is an increasingly relevant concern as more training data is itself generated by other LLMs, which may have been influenced by exposure to benchmark content during their own training or generation process.

explainer.lead: Synthetic benchmark contamination happens when AI-generated training data unknowingly carries content from benchmark test sets. It matters because scores can then look better than true generalisation warrants.

tiers.eli5: It's like studying from a practice test that secretly contains the real exam's questions — your score stops telling the truth.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers building training sets from other models' outputs must screen for benchmark overlap; the pitfall is indirect leakage, since a generator model may itself have absorbed benchmark content during its own training.
tiers.paperLevel: There is no standard formal measure; the concern is that contamination is harder to detect than in direct scraping because the leaking content has been rephrased or regenerated by an intermediate model.

explainer.example: A team generates reasoning problems with an LLM to fine-tune a model, unaware that some regenerated items mirror questions from a widely used evaluation set, inflating the reported score.
